text.p: Tropical storm Fern is becoming an increasing risk to shipping in the region well east of the southern Philippines. Top winds are already at 60 mph and should reach 75 mph in 24 hours. Further strengthening is likely through 48 hours before slightly weakening begins. The system tracks north and then northeast this weekend. This track is mostly over open water for 48 hours before it threatens the northern Mariana islands after that.

Tropical cyclone Fergus is also an increasing risk to shipping in the eastern Coral Sea to the east of Australia. Top winds are currently about 50 mph and they should reach 75 mph in 24 hours. Movement towards the south should keep the system over open water through the 48 hour period.
Tropical depression 43w is only a minor risk to shipping in the South China Sea to the west of Sabah, Malaysia. Top winds are only 35 mph and little change in strength is expected this period.
Tropical cyclone 12p is also of some risk to shipping in the Gulf of Carpentaria this period. Winds are about 35 mph at this time but they may reach 45 mph in 24 hours.
